### Content
- **Description**: The screen displays a media transcription and subtitle editing interface. The layout is horizontally divided mainly into three areas: the left panel, the central text and media area, and the bottom timeline area. On the left panel, there is a 'Comments' section showing user comments with small avatar thumbnails and timestamps in grayscale text. The main central area presents a vertical text transcript in black font on a white background, with sections of the transcript highlighted with a red border and background to indicate selection or editing. The text is in a serif font, approximately 14-16px size, black (#000000) on white (#FFFFFF). Below the text block in the center is a media control bar featuring a circular play button flanked by rewind and forward icons and a speed control option labeled '1.0x'. The time indicator '0:36 / 4:17' is clearly visible, showing current playback and total duration. Above the transcript is a file name bar showing 'time_machine_story.pdf' indicating the source media. On the right side of the transcript is a vertical playback progress bar with a small horizontal handle slider. At the bottom part of the screen is a horizontal timeline representing the transcript aligned with audio, segmented into blocks with textual annotations. These blocks are labeled with transcription snippets and corresponding audio descriptions, such as '5-second magical sparkle sound fade' and 'A gentle, continuous, 30-second subtle'. The timeline's color scheme uses shades of light red and blue for different annotation types. A tooltip or modal is visible on the right top, labeled 'Export' with options for media type selection (set to 'Video'), and information about watermark and cost to generate remaining paragraphs text in grey on black (#000000 background, #FFFFFF text). Buttons are rectangular with grey strokes. Overall, the style is minimalist and clean, using a neutral color palette dominated by black, white, grey with accent colors (red and blue) in the timeline annotations. The layout is well-structured with clear alignment and consistent spacing. Buttons and icons are flat and modern with no 3D effects or shadows. The interface supports user interaction with media playback, text editing/highlighting, commenting, and exporting functionality. There are no visible animations in the screenshot, but media playback controls indicate dynamic media behavior. The interface uses left-aligned text blocks and bottom-aligned timeline with horizontal linear flow. Vertical navigation and interaction is enabled in comment and transcript panels.
- **Layout**: The layout consists of three main vertical sections and one bottom horizontal section. From left to right: a narrow left sidebar (approximately 15% width) dedicated to comments with a vertical list, a central wide column (approximately 55% width) containing the transcript and media controls stacked vertically, and a right narrow column (approximately 10%) showing vertical playback progress and timeline controls. The bottom section spans the full width horizontally and presents a segmented timeline with labeled audio/text blocks, sized to represent duration. The layout uses a single-column main content area with fixed sidebars for comments and controls. Elements are arranged with ample padding (~20px) around text blocks. Horizontal alignment is consistent with left edges aligned for text and timeline. Vertical stacking for media controls below transcript ensures logical reading flow. The timeline is segmented into multiple blocks representing speech and sound effects (estimate 8-10 segments visible horizontally). The entire layout is clean and grid-based with consistent gutters between columns and timeline blocks. Layout keywords: sidebar, vertical column, horizontal timeline, segmented blocks, media controls, dual-panel, responsive grid, stacked elements, timeline alignment, comment panel.
- **Functions**: Users can interact with the transcription text by selecting, editing, and highlighting parts of the transcript, as indicated by red-bordered highlighted text segments. The play button and timeline allow precise control of media playback, enabling users to listen to specific audio or video segments and synchronize text with audiovisual content. The speed control (1.0x) suggests users can adjust playback speed for easier transcription verification or editing. Comments section enables users to add, read, and search comments related to specific timecodes or transcript segments to facilitate collaborative review and discussion. The timeline at the bottom provides a visual representation of audio/video segments synchronized with transcript snippets and sound effects, allowing users to accurately place or tweak subtitle timings and audio annotations. Export functionality supports users to generate and save the edited media, with options to choose media type and manage watermark settings, enabling finalization of subtitle or transcript projects. Broader purpose is to create, edit, and manage subtitles or transcripts aligned with media content efficiently, ensuring high accuracy and easy collaboration for multimedia production, transcription review, and content localization workflows. The interface aids clarity by visually linking transcription text, audio/video playback, and user annotations through an integrated timeline, controls, and comment system.

### Content
- **Description**: The screen shows a sophisticated multimedia editing interface tailored for video editing. The layout is horizontally divided into three main sections: a left sidebar, a central content panel, and a bottom timeline panel. The left sidebar vertically stacks multiple labeled buttons such as Edit, SFX, Music, Video (highlighted), Imports, Caption, and Comments with monochrome icons, on a white background. Below these, a video clip thumbnail is visible with the label 'Generated Video' and a duration stamp (00:05). The central content panel contains a vertical scrollable text block that functions as a transcript or script editor with black text on white background, in a readable serif font, approximately 16px. On the right side of the content panel, there is a video playback preview window showing a person's headshot labeled 'Original' with subtle border and shadowing and a playhead control below. The bottom timeline panel spans full width, showing a timeline from 0:20s to 0:48s with precise segmentation. The timeline displays rectangular segments with layered labels in red and blue colors representing subtitles or caption blocks. Text snippets inside these blocks represent spoken words and sound effect cues. The timeline includes playhead controls with a black play/pause button centered, playback speed control (currently 1.0x), and time indicator (0:39 / 4:17). The bottom right has zoom and audio volume sliders. The UI uses a monochromatic color palette dominated by white backgrounds (#FFFFFF), light grays (#F0F0F0) for panel separation, black (#000000) for text and controls, subtle blue (#1A73E8) for highlights on selected timeline blocks, and red (#D93025) for marked transcript lines. Typography is clear and functional, blending a serif font for the transcript (e.g., Times New Roman or Georgia) and a sans-serif for UI controls (e.g., Roboto or Arial). The design is minimal, with flat UI elements, subtle shadows on interactive components, and consistent spacing of roughly 16-20px padding between sections. The overall style is professional and utilitarian suited for editors working on video transcription, captioning, and video light editing. Animations likely include smooth timeline scrubbing and real-time playback synchronization with subtitles. The screen layout uses a three-column structure with the left navigation column narrow, a wide central reading pane, and a narrow media preview column, and a horizontal multi-track timeline panel at the bottom.
- **Layout**: The layout is a three-column structure with a horizontal timeline strip below. The left column is a narrow vertical sidebar containing navigation buttons stacked vertically. The middle column is the largest, featuring a vertically scrollable text area with multiline paragraphs aligned left, occupying most of the vertical space. The right column is a slimmer vertical panel housing the video playback preview. The bottom area spans full width beneath these three columns and is dedicated to the timeline with segmented blocks arranged horizontally in a single row representing time from roughly 0s to 48s with playhead visible. Padding is consistent around each major section (approx. 16-20px). The timeline includes layered text blocks with color coding (red and blue), and timeline controls centered beneath the main timeline. The interface uses a fixed-width grid arrangement for the timeline and flexible column widths for the main three panes. The timeline is a single-row segmented track containing multiple labeled blocks with text overlays and subtle dividing lines for each segment. The screen overall is structured in horizontal bands with vertical columns above and a bottom fixed horizontal track. Visual hierarchy and alignment focus on clarity of text editing and synchronization with video preview.
- **Functions**: Users can select video clips to edit from the left sidebar, with the interface focused on video and caption editing. They can read and edit the transcript text in the central panel, with precise audio-video synchronization visible in the timeline below. The timeline allows users to manipulate subtitle caption blocks by resizing and moving them, supported by color-coded cues for clarity. Video playback controls permit previewing the video at different timestamps and speeds. Users can zoom in/out on the timeline to fine-tune subtitle timing. The bottom timeline highlights sections of speech or effects, enabling editing of subtitles and sound effects alongside the video. The interface facilitates workflows like creating and adjusting video captions, syncing subtitle text to spoken audio, adding or modifying sound effects durations, and previewing changes in real time. Overall, the screen enables video editors or content creators to produce accurately captioned, accessible videos with integrated audio and subtitle control, ensuring precision and efficiency in video transcription and multimedia production.

### Content
- **Description**: Overall style and layout
- Clean, modern, productivity-focused video editor layout with soft neutral backgrounds, white panels and a vivid purple primary accent. Visual language aligns with Microsoft design: generous white space, rounded corners, flat icons, subtle shadows and thin separators.

Structure
- Three main vertical areas (left, center, right) inside a full-width canvas with a top control bar spanning the full width. Left column (media/library) is narrow, center column (preview + timeline) is wide and dominant, right column (tool/properties) is narrow.
- Left column width: ~260px. Center column flexible, occupying the remaining width minus right column. Right column width: ~140px. Top bar height: ~44px.

Background and surfaces
- Page background: very light gray (#F6F6F7 / RGB 246,246,247).
- Panel backgrounds: solid white (#FFFFFF). Panels have 8px corner radius and very subtle drop shadow (RGBA(16,24,40,0.03)) or 1px soft border (#E6E6E9).

Typography
- Primary font: Segoe UI / Inter / system sans. Base body size: 14px regular (400). Headings / labels: 16–18px semibold (600). Timecodes and small UI: 12px / 13px regular. Line-height 1.3–1.5 depending on element. Text alignment mostly left; center for preview captions/timecode.

Primary colors (approximate)
- Primary / Brand purple (buttons, selection): #6F2BD9 (RGB 111,43,217).
- Strong purple accent (hover / active): #7C3AED (RGB 124,58,237).
- Light purple selection / timeline range: #F3E8FF or #EDE6FF (RGB ~243,232,255 / 237,230,255) at 30–40% opacity for fills.
- Neutral grays: text primary #111827 (near-black), secondary text #6B7280 (gray-500), borders / separators #E6E7EA.
- Playhead / controls black: #111827.

Preview / Canvas
- Large video preview centered in the top half of the center column. Preview aspect ratio ~16:9 within a white canvas containing a faint selection outline when clip is selected. Selection outline is 3px solid purple (#6F2BD9) with small circular drag handles at corners (8–12px) and a rotate handle centered on top (if visible).
- Canvas has small toolbar floating above or inside the preview (button cluster) containing crop/transform/fit icons in a light rounded rectangle (height ~36px, padding 6px).
- A light play button sits centered under the preview (circular, 44–56px diameter, dark icon on white or dark circular background), with timecode displayed next to it (e.g., 0:47 / 0:47).

Timeline
- Timeline located directly under the preview. Contains a horizontal scrubber/time ruler with ticks every few seconds and highlighted time region segments. Ruler text uses 12px monospace-like timecode.
- Video track shows a long strip of frame thumbnails. Thumbnails are contained in the video track row, about 64px height for the thumbnail strip. Track container has soft rounded corners and purple handles at each end to indicate selected clip boundaries (8px radius handles, filled purple #6F2BD9).
- Playhead: vertical black line (~2px width) spanning preview height and timeline, with a round draggable head/knob at the top (16px diameter). The playhead has a slight shadow and snaps to thumbnails/frames.
- Audio track sits below the video track showing a faint waveform in light gray (#CBD5E1). Track heights: video track ~72–88px, audio track ~36–48px. Spacing between tracks ~12–16px.
- Timeline background: white with subtle 1px separators. Timeline zoom/controls (zoom in/out, fit, timeline settings) appear bottom-right of the timeline section as small icon buttons (24–32px square).

Left column (Media / Library)
- Header with product name (left of top bar) and a purple primary CTA: "Import media" button (prominent purple rectangle with white text, rounded corners 8px, padding 8–10px vertical, 12–16px horizontal). The button includes a small upload icon to the left.
- Below CTA is a vertical list / grid of media thumbnails (media gallery). Each media item shows thumbnail image, small duration badge bottom-left (dark translucent badge with white 12px text), and filename or short label below the thumbnail in 12–13px grey text.
- Left list has 8–10px vertical spacing, subtle hover highlight (light gray background) and small checkboxes or selection indicators on hover.

Right column (Tools / Effects / Properties)
- Narrow vertical toolbar of icons (Filters, Effects, Adjust, Speed, etc.) arranged as a vertical stack, each icon inside a circular or rounded square button (~40px). Icons use line-style minimal glyphs, inactive icons are gray (#9CA3AF), active icons display purple accent.
- When a tool is active, the right column shows its panel with controls (sliders, toggles, presets). Controls include small sliders (track height 4px, thumb 12px), toggles (rounded switches), and select lists. Labels at 13–14px.

Top-right controls
- Shared / Export functionality: "Share" small text button and a prominent "Export" primary button in purple (#6F2BD9) with white label, 10–12px vertical padding, 14–16px label, right-aligned in top bar. User avatar circular at far right (~32px) with small drop-down for account menu.

Icons & micro-interactions
- Buttons have hover states: primary button darkens to #7C3AED. Secondary buttons use 1px border #E6E7EA and text color #374151, hover background #F3F4F6.
- Drag & drop interactions: thumbnails highlight with dotted border and subtle ghost preview when dragging. Clip trimming handles show grab cursor and change thickness on hover. Playhead drags smoothly with 120–200ms easing.

Spacing & alignment
- Global spacing: 16px gutters between columns, 12–16px internal paddings. Left column inner padding ~12px. Center canvas uses 24px padding from top bar.

States & feedback
- Selected clip: purple outline, purple handles, and timeline segment tinted faint purple. Disabled/empty track state: faint dashed placeholder with "+ Add audio" text.
- Loader / skeleton: when assets load, thumbnails use grey rectangles skeleton with shimmer.

Recreation notes
- Use modular components: left media panel (vertical list of cards), top preview card, timeline strip with layered tracks and playhead, right properties vertical panel. Keep consistent radii (8px), neutral grays and a single strong purple accent. Ensure the timeline is interactive: draggable playhead, clip handles, thumbnails, and audio waveform beneath.
- **Layout**: High-level layout
- Three-column layout with one topbar: left media column (1), central editor column (2), right tools column (3). The topbar is full-width across the three columns.

Columns and groups
- Left column (1) — single vertical group containing: top header (Import media CTA), then a scrollable media gallery/list that displays rectangular thumbnails in a single-column list. This left column contains 1 group.
- Center column (2) — split vertically into two main stacked groups: an upper preview group (video canvas, floating preview toolbar, play/pause control and timecode) and a lower timeline group (time ruler, video track with thumbnails, audio track with waveform, timeline controls). The center column contains 2 stacked groups.
- Right column (3) — vertical tools toolbar group (icon stack) and below that a property panel area that expands depending on the selected tool. This right column contains 1 group but can expand to multiple sub-sections.

Timeline grid details
- The timeline is a horizontal grid made of rows (tracks). Count: typically 2 visible tracks in this screen: Video track (row 1) and Audio track (row 2). Each track is horizontally continuous across the center column. Key elements within the timeline: left/right purple handles (clip boundaries), thumbnails repeated across the clip's width (approx 10–12 thumbs visible in this screenshot), and the vertical playhead that intersects both rows.

Alignment & padding
- Column gutters ~16px. Panel paddings: 12–16px. Topbar padding left/right 12–20px. Playhead centered vertically across preview and timeline when scrubbed. Visual alignment uses a baseline grid for 8px increments.

Keywords to describe layout and structure
- three-column
- left-sidebar
- center-canvas
- right-toolbar
- top-navbar
- timeline-strip
- thumbnail-track
- vertical-playhead
- stacked-groups
- responsive-center
- **Functions**: Specific actions (lowest level)
- Click "Import media" to upload files (opens file picker or drag/drop target). The button shows primary purple styling and an upload icon.
- Select a media thumbnail in the left media list to insert it into the timeline or preview it in the canvas. Thumbnails show duration badges and hover states.
- Drag and drop media from the left library into the timeline track or directly onto the preview canvas. Dragging displays a translucent ghost of the clip and highlights the drop target in purple.
- Play / pause the project using the central play control (circular play button) and observe current timecode. The playhead moves across the timeline while playing.
- Drag the vertical playhead to scrub/scrub through frames. The preview updates in real time to the frame under the playhead.
- Trim clips using drag handles at either end of the clip in the timeline. Handles are purple when active and show precise time markers while trimming.
- Add audio by clicking "+ Add audio" in the audio track area; audio waveform is displayed once added and can be trimmed or moved independently.
- Open the right-hand tool panel icons (Filters, Effects, Adjust, Speed) to modify clip properties using sliders, toggles, and presets. Controls show immediate preview updates.
- Use timeline zoom controls (magnifying icons) bottom-right to zoom in/out on the timeline. The thumbnail density increases/decreases accordingly.
- Export or Share the finished video via the top-right "Export" button; a modal or panel presents export settings (resolution, codec, quality) and progress indicator.

Medium-level tasks (workflows)
- Create a sequence: select multiple clips from the media library and assemble them onto the timeline in order, trim start/end points, and reposition clips by dragging.
- Edit audio independently: add an audio file, align it to the video track, trim audio, adjust volume with a slider in the right-hand properties, and observe waveform changes.
- Add overlays and text: insert a text layer above the video track ("+ Add text" placeholder visible), edit font properties (size, weight, color) in the right panel, and position the overlay inside the preview.
- Apply visual effects: open the Filters panel and apply an effect preset; tweak intensity using a slider and preview results immediately in the canvas.
- Fine tune clip timing: nudge clips left/right on the timeline, snap to playhead or neighbor clip edges. Use timeline zoom to perform frame-accurate cuts.
- Preview and iterate: scrub/play the timeline repeatedly, make adjustments, and use undo/redo controls (not explicitly pictured but typically present) to revert changes.

Broad purpose (highest level)
- The screen is a lightweight video editing workspace whose overall purpose is to let users import media, assemble and trim clips on a timeline, add audio and overlays, apply effects, preview the result, and export/share the final video. The interface is optimized for quick editing tasks (cutting, trimming, arranging), with clear visual affordances for drag-and-drop, immediate visual feedback in the preview, and streamlined export controls to finish the editing workflow efficiently.
